title: PSG-Q4: fourth-root source growth with polynomial storage

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG-Q4 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its total charged sequential work obeys T(N,s)=O(n^(11/4) (log2 n)^(11/4) 2^((1/2)(n log2 n)^(3/4))). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_T(n)=n^(11/4) (log2 n)^(11/4) 2^((1/2)(n log2 n)^(3/4)), for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 3/4. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG-Q4 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its peak classical bits obeys S_C(N,s)=O(n^2). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_S_C(n)=n^2, for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG-Q4 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its peak qubits obeys S_Q(N,s)=O(n). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_S_Q(n)=n, for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single PSG-Q4 algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md, including its source and weighted-attempt cutoffs, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures and aborts, its total acquired source copies, including all failed and discarded copies obeys Q(N,s)=O(n^(7/4) (log2 n)^(3/4) 2^((4/5)(n log2 n)^(1/4))). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_Q(n)=n^(7/4) (log2 n)^(3/4) 2^((4/5)(n log2 n)^(1/4)), for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 1/4. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For the same PSG-Q4 algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
